title: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach
content_md: Hackers have reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, adding to a recent wave of cyberattacks affecting US government agencies, including the FBI, CIA, and Treasury Department. According to Reuters , the intrusion was discovered within the past month during an upgrade of the cloud platform, disrupting application migrations and software updates. Launched in 2017, Cloud One is an enterprise cloud computing platform managed by the US Air Force that allows Department of Defense agencies to host and manage applications supporting military operations, personnel management, logistics, and maintenance. According to one source who spoke to Reuters, the hackers exploited an unidentified software vulnerability to gain access to the platform, potentially exposing sensitive military operational and logistics information. US Cyber Command has reportedly been called in to assess the impact, with the attackers, scope of the attack, and whether any data was stolen currently unknown. The Air Force declined to comment on the security or operational status of the affected systems, telling Reuters that it continuously takes measures to protect its information, systems, and mission capabilities. The reported Air Force breach follows other cybersecurity incidents disclosed over the past week targeting US federal agencies.
